title: Wrap, fasten and set down a folded umbrella
instruction: Wrap the loose tie around the folded umbrella, press it closed and lay the fastened umbrella on the table.
context: A collapsed umbrella springs loose in a bag unless its tie is wrapped and fastened. People usually turn the bundle with the handle hand while the other keeps the fabric gathered, guides the tie and presses the fastener; any way of wrapping that leaves it gathered, fastened and holding after release counts.
setup: Two YAM arms, an ordinary flat table and a folded compact umbrella with a 239 × 24 mm strap, a 55 mm hook region and a 72 mm loop region. The handle starts in the left gripper and the right gripper begins open.
scoring: End-state score; how the tie is wound and which hand acts are not scored. 0.25: canopy gathered to ≤80% of its loose shaft-centred diameter (end-on photo, ruler) while held in a gripper or resting on the table. 0.50: also the tie ≥270° round the shaft. 0.75: also ≥365° round with visible overlap and the hook patch engaged on the loop patch (photo). 1.00: also lowered onto the table, not dropped (it rests on the table before the last gripper opens; side video), both grippers ≥20 mm clear and not touching it, and once released the wrap stays gathered, wound and fastened with nothing moving for 1 s, still so at the end. Otherwise 0.
reset_notes: Settle the preheld handle and freely hanging strap under gravity before the episode.
fidelity: A free shaft, twelve sprung canopy sections and fifteen hinged strap sections approximate folded fabric. Hook-and-loop engages when overlapping, aligned patches are pressed at ≥0.15 N for three controls by either gripper; bonded areas can peel or shear apart. Pad and table contact forces and clearance verify holding and release. The demo reads simulator poses, contact forces and the fastener state, never the score. Material constants are uncalibrated.
